title.suggested: Johnny Dwyer Says He Wants to Fight Tom Allen

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican printed a Buffalo report after Johnny Dwyer beat Jimmy Elliott, in which Dwyer said Tom Allen had maligned him and he would go to England to fight him.

metadata.notes: Masthead: 'The Republican: St. Louis, Sunday Morning, May 11, 1879', page 12. Filed as Missouri Republican (before 1888). Item reprinted from the Cincinnati Enquirer's Buffalo correspondent, dated May 9.

facts.fact: After beating Jimmy Elliott, Johnny Dwyer said he wanted to fight one more man, Tom Allen, who he said had maligned him; he offered to go to England to fight him and to send £10 to the editor of Bell's Life in London as a forfeit for a match
Jimmy Elliott, said to hate Allen, said he was glad it was Dwyer and not Allen who beat him, and hoped Dwyer would fight Allen, promising to back Dwyer

notes: Dwyer and Elliott quotes are theirs, not Allen's, so quote fields are blank. Dwyer's remark implies Allen was in England at the time.
